title.en: Volume 181 Biographies 106: Chen, three Li's, Cao, Liu

sentences.zh: 陳三李曹劉

translations.literal: Chen, three Li's, Cao, Liu
translations.idiomatic: Chen, the three Lis, Cao, and Liu

sentences.zh: ◎陳夷行李紳李讓夷曹確劉瞻

translations.literal: ◎ Chen Yixing, Li Shen, Li Rangyi, Cao Que, Liu Zhan
translations.idiomatic: ◎ Chen Yixing, Li Shen, Li Rangyi, Cao Que, and Liu Zhan

translations.literal: (Zhu)
translations.idiomatic: (Liu Zhu)

sentences.zh: 李蔚

translations.literal: Li Wei
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei

sentences.zh: 陳夷行，字周道，其先江左諸陳也，世客潁川。

translations.literal: Chen Yixing, styled Zhoudao, his ancestors were the various Chens of the Jiangzuo region, for generations sojourning in Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yixing, courtesy name Zhoudao, was descended from the Chen clans of the lower Yangtze; his family had long resided as guests in Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 由進士第，擢累起居郎、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Through the jinshi degree, he was repeatedly promoted to Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Having passed the jinshi examination, he rose through successive appointments as Attendant of the Heir Apparent and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 以勞遷司封員外郎，凡再歲，以吏部郎中為翰林學士。

translations.literal: For merit he was transferred to Vice Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments; in all two years, as Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Civil Office he became a Hanlin Academician.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was moved to Vice Director of the Bureau of Enfeoffments; after two years he entered the Hanlin Academy as a Bachelor while serving as Director of Personnel in the Ministry of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 莊恪太子在東宮，夷行兼侍讀，五日一謁，為太子講說。

translations.literal: When the Zhuangke Heir Apparent was in the Eastern Palace, Yixing concurrently served as Lecturer, every five days one audience, lecturing for the heir.
translations.idiomatic: While the Zhuangke Heir Apparent resided in the Eastern Palace, Yixing also served as Lecturer, attending every five days to instruct the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 數遷至工部侍郎。

translations.literal: Repeatedly transferred up to Vice Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages until he reached Vice Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 開成二年，進同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaicheng, he advanced to Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In 837 he was appointed Associate Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 而楊嗣復、李玨相次輔政，夷行介特，雅不與合，每議論天子前，往往語相侵短。

translations.literal: But Yang Sifu and Li Jue in succession assisted government; Yixing was upright and exceptional, by nature not in accord with them, and whenever they debated before the Son of Heaven their words often mutually cut short.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Sifu and Li Jue were then serving in turn as chief ministers. Yixing was stiff and uncompromising by nature and had little use for them; whenever they debated policy before the emperor their exchanges often turned into personal attacks.

sentences.zh: 夷行不能堪，輒引疾求去，文宗遣使者尉勞起之。

translations.literal: Yixing could not bear it, then citing illness sought to leave; Emperor Wenzong sent envoys to console and comfort him and raise him up.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to endure this, Yixing repeatedly pleaded illness to resign, whereupon Emperor Wenzong sent envoys to console him and recall him to office.

sentences.zh: 會以王彥威為忠武節度使，史孝章領邠寧，議皆出嗣復。

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Yanwei was made Military Commissioner of Zhongwu and Shi Xiaozhang took command of Binning; the deliberations all came from Sifu.
translations.idiomatic: About this time Wang Yanwei was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhongwu and Shi Xiaozhang was put in charge of Binning—decisions that had all originated with Sifu.

sentences.zh: 及夷行對延英，帝問：「除二鎮當否？

translations.literal: When Yixing responded at Yanying, the emperor asked: "Are the appointments to the two circuits appropriate?
translations.idiomatic: When Yixing appeared for audience in the Yanying Hall, the emperor asked, "Were these two frontier appointments appropriate?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「茍自聖擇，無不當者。

translations.literal: " He replied: "If from the sage's own choice, there is none not appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: " He answered, "If Your Majesty chose them yourself, they cannot fail to be right.

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「若用人盡出上意而當，固善。

translations.literal: " Sifu said: "If employing men entirely from the sovereign's intent and they fit, that is indeed good.
translations.idiomatic: " Sifu said, "If every appointment came straight from Your Majesty's will and proved correct, that would be fine.

sentences.zh: 如小不稱，下安得嘿然？

translations.literal: If slightly not fitting, how can subordinates keep silent?
translations.idiomatic: But if they are even slightly unsuitable, how can your ministers remain silent?

sentences.zh: 」夷行曰：「比奸臣數幹權，願陛下無倒持大阿，以鐏授人。

translations.literal: " Yixing said: "Of late treacherous ministers repeatedly meddled with power; I wish Your Majesty not to hold the great axe reversed and hand the haft to others.
translations.idiomatic: " Yixing said, "Treacherous ministers have repeatedly seized power of late. I beg Your Majesty not to hold the great axe by the blade and hand the haft to someone else.

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「古者任則不疑，齊桓公器管仲於讎虜，豈有倒持慮邪？

translations.literal: " Sifu said: "In antiquity once one appoints one does not doubt; Duke Huan of Qi valued Guan Zhong from among enemy captives—how could there be concern about holding reversed?
translations.idiomatic: " Sifu replied, "In antiquity to appoint was to trust without doubt. Duke Huan of Qi prized Guan Zhong even though he had been a captive of his enemies—why should there be any fear of handing over authority?

sentences.zh: 」帝以其面相觸，頗不悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor because their faces opposed each other was quite displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, seeing them clash face to face, was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 仙韶樂工尉遲璋授王府率，右拾遺竇洵直當衙論奏，鄭覃、嗣復嫌以細故，謂洵直近名。

translations.literal: A Xianzhao musician, Yuchi Zhang, was given the post of Commandant of the Princely Household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi at court memorialized in debate; Zheng Tan and Sifu resented it as a petty matter and said Xunzhi was courting fame.
translations.idiomatic: A musician of the Xianzhao Office, Yuchi Zhang, was appointed Commandant of the Princely Household. Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi memorialized at court against the appointment. Zheng Tan and Sifu dismissed it as trivial and accused Xunzhi of seeking renown.

sentences.zh: 夷行曰：「諫官當衙，正須論宰相得失，彼賤工安足言者？

translations.literal: Yixing said: "Remonstrance officials at court ought precisely to discuss the chancellors' gains and losses—how are those base artisans worth speaking of?
translations.idiomatic: Yixing said, "It is precisely a remonstrance official's duty at court to discuss the chancellors' merits and faults. What business has a lowly artisan here?

sentences.zh: 然亦不可置不用。

translations.literal: Yet also one cannot set him aside and not use him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he should not be ignored altogether.

sentences.zh: 」帝即徙璋光州長史，以百縑賜洵直。

translations.literal: " The emperor at once transferred Zhang to Long Prefecture as Administrator and gave Xunzhi a hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor immediately transferred Zhang to the post of Administrator of Guang Prefecture and rewarded Xunzhi with a hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 進門下侍郎。

translations.literal: He advanced to Vice Minister of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Minister of the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 帝常怪天寶政事不善，問：「姚元崇、宋璟於時在否？

translations.literal: The emperor often wondered that Tianbao government affairs were not good and asked: "Were Yao Chong and Song Jing present at that time?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often lamented that government under the Tianbao era had gone wrong and asked, "Were Yao Chong and Song Jing still in office then?

sentences.zh: 」李玨曰：「姚亡而宋罷。

translations.literal: " Li Jue said: "Yao had died and Song was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Jue said, "Yao was dead and Song had already been removed.

sentences.zh: 」玨因推言：「玄宗自謂未嘗殺一不辜，而任李林甫，種夷數十族，不亦惑乎？

translations.literal: " Jue then extended the saying: "Emperor Xuanzong himself claimed never to have killed one innocent person, yet he employed Li Linfu, who exterminated dozens of clans to the roots—is that not deluded?
translations.idiomatic: " Jue went on, "Emperor Xuanzong claimed he had never put an innocent man to death, yet he entrusted Li Linfu, who wiped out dozens of clans root and branch—is that not delusion?

sentences.zh: 」夷行曰：「陛下今亦宜戒以權屬人。

translations.literal: " Yixing said: "Your Majesty today also ought to take warning about vesting power in others.
translations.idiomatic: " Yixing said, "Your Majesty today should likewise take warning against handing power to others.

sentences.zh: 」嗣復曰：「夷行失言，太宗易暴亂為仁義，用房玄齡十有六年，任魏徵十有五年，未嘗失道。

translations.literal: " Sifu said: "Yixing misspoke. Taizong changed violence and disorder into benevolence and righteousness, employed Fang Xuanling for sixteen years and entrusted Wei Zheng for fifteen years, and never lost the Way.
translations.idiomatic: " Sifu said, "Yixing has spoken wrongly. Taizong turned violence and chaos into benevolent rule; he kept Fang Xuanling for sixteen years and Wei Zheng for fifteen, and never strayed from the right path.

sentences.zh: 人主用忠良久益治，用邪佞一日多矣。

translations.literal: A ruler employing the loyal for long brings increasing order; employing the wicked and fawning for a day brings much harm.
translations.idiomatic: When a ruler keeps loyal men long, government grows steadier day by day; employ the wicked and fawning for even a day and harm multiplies.

sentences.zh: 」時用郭薳為坊州刺史，右拾遺宋元阝論不可，果坐贓敗。

translations.literal: " At the time Guo Shen was used as Prefect of Fang Prefecture; Remonstrance Official Song Kuang argued it was not permissible, and indeed he was convicted on corruption and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Guo Shen was appointed Prefect of Fang Prefecture. Remonstrance Official Song Kuang argued against it, and Guo was indeed later ruined by a corruption conviction.

sentences.zh: 帝欲賞邧，夷行曰：「諫官論事是其職，若一事善輒進官，恐後不免有私。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to reward Kuang; Yixing said: "For remonstrance officials to debate affairs is their duty; if for one good matter they are promptly advanced in office, I fear later they cannot avoid partiality.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to reward Kuang. Yixing said, "It is a remonstrance official's duty to speak on policy. If every sound memorial earns a promotion, later remonstrators will hardly avoid self-interest.

sentences.zh: 」夷行蓋專詆嗣復。

translations.literal: " Yixing in general was solely slandering Sifu.
translations.idiomatic: " In truth Yixing was chiefly aiming his barbs at Sifu.

sentences.zh: 又素善覃，陰助其力，以排折朋黨。

translations.literal: He also had long been on good terms with Tan and secretly aided his strength to break and bend the factional cliques.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been friendly with Zheng Tan as well and secretly bolstered him in order to break the power of the factional cliques.

sentences.zh: 是時，雖天子亦惡其太過，恩禮遂衰，罷為吏部尚書，尋拜華州刺史。

translations.literal: At this time, even the Son of Heaven disliked his excess; favor and ceremony then declined; he was dismissed as Minister of Civil Office and soon appointed Governor of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: By then even the emperor had come to dislike his excesses. Imperial favor waned, and he was removed to the post of Minister of Civil Office, then soon made Governor of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，召為御史大夫，俄還門下侍郎平章事，進位尚書左仆射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, he was summoned as Censor-in-Chief; soon he returned as Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Grand Councillor, advancing to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Yixing was recalled as Censor-in-Chief, soon restored as Vice Minister of the Chancellery and Grand Councillor, and promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 夷行與崔珙俱拜，乃奏：「仆射始視事，受四品官拜，無著令。

translations.literal: Yixing and Cui Gong were both invested together and then memorialized: "When a Vice Director first assumes duties, receiving bows from fourth-rank officials—there is no established ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: When Yixing and Cui Gong took office together they submitted a memorial: "When a Vice Director first assumes his duties and receives bows from fourth-rank officials, there is no statute on the books for it.

sentences.zh: 比日左右丞、吏部侍郎、御史中丞皆為仆射拜階下，謂之『隔品致敬』。

translations.literal: In recent days the Left and Right Assistant Directors, Vice Ministers of Civil Office, and Vice Censor-in-Chief all bow to the Vice Director below the steps—called 'homage across ranks.'
translations.idiomatic: Lately the Left and Right Assistant Directors, the Vice Ministers of Civil Office, and the Vice Censor-in-Chief have all bowed to the Vice Director at the foot of the steps—what is called 'homage across ranks.'

sentences.zh: 準禮，皇太子見上臺群官，群官先拜而後答，以無二上也。

translations.literal: According to ritual, when the Crown Prince sees the superior terrace group of officials, the group of officials bow first and then respond, because there is no second superior.
translations.idiomatic: By ritual, when the crown prince receives officials of the upper terrace, the officials bow first and he responds afterward, for there cannot be two superiors.

sentences.zh: 仆射與四品官並列朝廷，不容獨優。

translations.literal: The Vice Director and fourth-rank officials stand together in court; one cannot allow him alone to be superior.
translations.idiomatic: A Vice Director stands in court on equal footing with fourth-rank officials; he cannot be granted privilege alone.

sentences.zh: 前日鄭餘慶著《仆射上儀》，謂隔品官無亢禮。

translations.literal: Previously Zheng Yuqing wrote the 'Ceremonial for Vice Directors at Court,' saying officials across ranks have no rite of refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zheng Yuqing had written Ceremonial for Vice Directors at Court, holding that officials of different ranks owed no deferential rite to one another.

sentences.zh: 時竇易直任御史中丞，議不可。

translations.literal: At the time Dou Yizhi held the post of Vice Censor-in-Chief and argued it was not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dou Yizhi was serving as Vice Censor-in-Chief and argued that this was improper.

sentences.zh: 及易直自為仆射，乃忘前議，當時鄙厭之。

translations.literal: When Yizhi himself became Vice Director, he then forgot his former argument; people at the time despised and detested this.
translations.idiomatic: But when Yizhi himself became Vice Director he forgot his earlier position, and contemporaries despised him for it.

sentences.zh: 臣等不願以失禮速誚於時。

translations.literal: Your subjects do not wish through loss of ritual quickly to be reproached by the age.
translations.idiomatic: We do not wish to invite swift reproach for breach of ritual.

sentences.zh: 且開元元年，以左右仆射為左右丞相，位次三公，三公上日答拜，而仆射受之，非是。

translations.literal: Moreover in the first year of Kaiyuan the Left and Right Vice Directors were made Left and Right Chancellors, ranking after the Three Dukes; on the Three Dukes' court days they returned bows, yet the Vice Directors received them—this is not correct.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in 713 the Left and Right Vice Directors were renamed Left and Right Chancellors and ranked just below the Three Dukes. On the Three Dukes' court days they return bows, yet Vice Directors receive them—that is wrong.

sentences.zh: 望敕所司約《三公上儀》，著定令。

translations.literal: We hope Your Majesty will order the responsible offices to follow the 'Ceremonial for the Three Dukes at Court' and fix it as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: We ask that Your Majesty order the responsible offices to follow Ceremonial for the Three Dukes at Court and codify the rule.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict approved their request.

sentences.zh: 始，累朝紛議不決，至夷行遂定。

translations.literal: At the beginning, for successive reigns confused debate did not decide; reaching Yixing it was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: For generations successive courts had debated the issue without resolution; Yixing finally settled it.

sentences.zh: 以足疾乞身，罷為太子太保，以檢校司空為河中節度使，卒。

translations.literal: Because of foot ailment he begged to retire from the body; he was dismissed as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and as Acting Minister of Works became Military Commissioner of Hedong, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness in his feet and asked to retire, was relieved as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, and served as Acting Minister of Works and Military Commissioner of Hedong until his death.

sentences.zh: 李紳，字公垂，中書令敬玄曾孫。

translations.literal: Li Shen, styled Gongchui, was the great-grandson of Grand Councillor Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shen, courtesy name Gongchui, was the great-grandson of Grand Councillor Li Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 世宦南方，客潤州。

translations.literal: For generations they served as officials in the south, sojourning in Run Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His family had served in office in the south for generations and lived as guests in Run Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紳六歲而孤，哀等成人。

translations.literal: Shen at six years was orphaned; in grief he was like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was orphaned at six and mourned with the gravity of a grown man.

sentences.zh: 母盧，躬授之學。

translations.literal: His mother Lu personally taught him learning.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, née Lu, taught him herself.

sentences.zh: 為人短小精悍，於詩最有名，時號「短李」。

translations.literal: As a man he was short in stature, keen and vigorous; in poetry he was most famous, and at the time was called 'Short Li.'
translations.idiomatic: He was short in stature but keen and forceful, and was most renowned for his poetry; contemporaries called him 'Short Li.'

sentences.zh: 蘇州刺史韋夏卿數稱之。

translations.literal: Suzhou Prefect Wei Xiaqing repeatedly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaqing, Prefect of Suzhou, often praised him.

sentences.zh: 葬母，有烏銜芝墜輔車。

translations.literal: When burying his mother, a crow carrying fungus fell onto the funeral carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At his mother's burial a crow carrying a fungus in its beak dropped it onto the funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 元和初，擢進士第，補國子助教，不樂，輒去。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was selected in the jinshi degree, appointed Assistant in the Directorate of Education, was not pleased, and promptly left.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanhe era he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed an assistant in the Directorate of Education, but he was unhappy in the post and soon resigned.

sentences.zh: 客金陵，李锜愛其才，辟掌書記。

translations.literal: Sojourning in Jinling, Li Qi loved his talent and summoned him as Chief Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: While living in Jinling he was admired by Li Qi, who engaged him as Chief Secretary.

sentences.zh: 锜浸不法，賓客莫敢言，紳數諫，不入；

translations.literal: Qi gradually became lawless; guests did not dare speak; Shen repeatedly remonstrated but it did not enter;
translations.idiomatic: Qi grew increasingly lawless. None of his retainers dared speak up, though Shen remonstrated repeatedly to no effect;

sentences.zh: 欲去，不許。

translations.literal: he wished to leave but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: when he tried to leave, Qi would not let him go.

sentences.zh: 會使者召锜，稱疾，留後王淡為具行，锜怒，陰教士臠食之，即脅使者為眾奏天子，幸得留。

translations.literal: It happened that envoys summoned Qi; he claimed illness; the acting commander Wang Dan made preparations to go; Qi was angry and secretly instructed soldiers to cut Dan to pieces and eat him, then coerced the envoy before the multitude to memorialize the Son of Heaven, and by luck was able to remain.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial envoys summoned Qi to court, he pleaded illness and had his deputy Wang Dan prepare to go in his stead. Qi, enraged, secretly ordered soldiers to hack Dan apart and devour him, then forced the envoy before the assembled troops to memorialize the throne on his behalf—and by luck was allowed to stay.

sentences.zh: 锜召紳作疏，坐锜前，紳陽怖栗，至不能為字，下筆輒塗去，盡數紙。

translations.literal: Qi summoned Shen to compose a memorial; seated before Qi, Shen pretended terror and trembling, to the point he could not form characters; whenever he set brush to paper he at once smeared it away, exhausting several sheets.
translations.idiomatic: Qi ordered Shen to draft the memorial and seated him before himself. Shen feigned such terror that he could not form a single character; every stroke he made he smeared away until he had ruined sheet after sheet.

sentences.zh: 锜怒罵曰：「何敢爾，不憚死邪？

translations.literal: Qi angrily cursed saying: "How dare you thus—are you not afraid of death?
translations.idiomatic: Qi raged and cursed, "How dare you behave like this—are you not afraid to die?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「生未嘗見金革，今得死為幸。

translations.literal: " He replied: "In life I have never seen arms and armor; now to obtain death is fortune.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "I have never known war in my life; to die now would be my good fortune.

sentences.zh: 」即註以刃，令易紙，復然。

translations.literal: " He was at once stabbed with a blade, ordered to change paper, and it was again so.
translations.idiomatic: " Qi had a blade pressed to him and ordered fresh paper, but Shen did the same again.

sentences.zh: 或言許縱能軍中書，紳不足用。

translations.literal: Someone said Xu Zong could write military documents; Shen was not sufficient to use.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said Xu Zong could handle military documents and that Shen was useless.

sentences.zh: 召縱至，操書如所欲，即囚紳獄中，锜誅，乃免。

translations.literal: Zong was summoned; wielding the brush as desired, Shen was then imprisoned in the jail; when Qi was executed, he was then released.
translations.idiomatic: Zong was summoned and wrote the memorial as Qi wished. Shen was thrown into prison and not released until Qi was executed.

sentences.zh: 或欲以聞，謝曰：「本激於義，非市名也。

translations.literal: Someone wished to report it to the court; he declined saying: "Originally I was stirred by righteousness, not trafficking in fame.
translations.idiomatic: Some wished to report his conduct to the court, but he declined, saying, "I acted from duty, not to buy a reputation.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: " Then it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " And so they desisted.

sentences.zh: 久之，從辟山南觀察府。

translations.literal: After long time, he followed recruitment into the Shannan Observation office.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he entered the staff of the Shannan Observation Commission.

sentences.zh: 穆宗召為右拾遺、翰林學士，與李德裕、元稹同時，號「三俊」。

translations.literal: Emperor Muzong summoned him as Right Remonstrance Official and Hanlin Academician; together with Li Deyu and Yuan Zhen at the same time, they were called 'the Three Outstanding Men.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Muzong summoned him as Right Remonstrance Official and Hanlin Academician. He served alongside Li Deyu and Yuan Zhen and was known as one of the 'Three Outstanding Men.'

sentences.zh: 累擢中書舍人。

translations.literal: Repeatedly promoted to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in stages to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 稹為宰相，而李逢吉教人告於方事，稹遂罷；

translations.literal: Zhen became Chancellor, but Li Fengji had someone accuse him in the Fang affair, and Zhen was then dismissed;
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Zhen became chancellor, Li Fengji had someone lodge charges against him in the Fang affair, and Zhen was removed;

sentences.zh: 欲引牛僧孺，懼紳等在禁近沮解，乃授德裕浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: wishing to bring in Niu Sengru, fearing Shen and others in close attendance at the forbidden precinct would obstruct and dissolve it, he then appointed Deyu Military Commissioner of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji wished to bring in Niu Sengru but feared that Shen and others near the throne would block the move, so he sent Li Deyu out as Military Commissioner of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 僧孺輔政，以紳為御史中丞，顧其氣剛卞，易疵累，而韓愈勁直，乃以愈為京兆尹，兼御史大夫，免臺參以激紳。

translations.literal: Sengru assisted government and made Shen Vice Censor-in-Chief, considering his spirit stiff and abrupt, easy to fault and entangle; while Han Yu was forceful and upright, he therefore made Yu Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao, concurrently Censor-in-Chief, exempting attendance at the Censorate to provoke Shen.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengru took power he appointed Shen Vice Censor-in-Chief, reckoning his temper stiff and abrasive and easy to trip up. Han Yu, however, was blunt and upright, so Sengru made Yu Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, exempting him from Censorate attendance in order to provoke Shen.

sentences.zh: 紳、愈果不相下，更持臺府故事，論詰往反，詆訐紛然，繇是皆罷之，以紳為江西觀察使。

translations.literal: Shen and Yu indeed did not yield to each other; they further held to Censorate precedents, arguing and questioning back and forth, slander and accusation in confusion; thereby both were dismissed, and Shen was made Military Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Yu would not yield to each other. They traded on Censorate precedent, arguing back and forth until mutual slander filled the court. Both were dismissed, and Shen was sent out as Military Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 帝素厚遇紳，遣使者就第勞賜，以為樂外遷，紳泣言為逢吉中傷。

translations.literal: The emperor had long treated Shen generously; he sent envoys to his residence to console and bestow gifts, thinking he was pleased at transfer outside; Shen wept saying he had been struck at the center by Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had always favored Shen and sent envoys to his home with gifts and words of comfort, assuming he welcomed an outside posting. Shen wept and said he had been struck down by Fengji's machinations.

sentences.zh: 入謝，又自陳所以然，帝悟，改戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Entering to give thanks, he again himself stated the reason why; the emperor understood and changed him to Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When he came to give thanks he explained the whole affair again, and the emperor understood; Shen was reassigned as Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 逢吉終欲陷之。

translations.literal: Fengji in the end wished to entrap him.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji still meant to destroy him in the end.

sentences.zh: 紳族子虞，有文學名，隱居華陽，自言不願仕，時來省紳，雅與柏耆、程昔範善。

translations.literal: Shen's clansman Yu had a literary reputation, dwelt in seclusion at Huayang, himself saying he did not wish to serve; he would come to visit Shen; he was by nature on good terms with Bai Qi and Cheng Xifan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen's clansman Li Yu had a literary reputation and lived in seclusion on Mount Hua, claiming he had no wish for office, though he visited Shen from time to time and was close to Bai Qi and Cheng Xifan.

sentences.zh: 及耆為拾遺，虞以書求薦，紳惡其無立操，痛誚之。

translations.literal: When Qi became Remonstrance Official, Yu by letter sought recommendation; Shen detested his lack of established integrity and bitterly reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When Bai Qi became a remonstrance official, Yu wrote asking Shen to recommend him. Shen despised his lack of principle and rebuked him harshly.

sentences.zh: 虞失望，後至京師，悉暴紳所言於逢吉。

translations.literal: Yu was disappointed; later he reached the capital and fully exposed Shen's words to Fengji.
translations.idiomatic: Disappointed, Yu later came to the capital and repeated everything Shen had said to Fengji.

sentences.zh: 逢吉滋怒，乃用張又新、李續等計，擢虞、昔範與劉棲楚皆為拾遺，以伺紳隙，內結中人王守澄自助。

translations.literal: Fengji grew more angry and then used Zhang Youxin, Li Xu, and others' plan, promoting Yu, Xifan, and Liu Qichu all as Remonstrance Officials to watch for openings in Shen, inwardly joining with the inner attendant Wang Shoucheng to assist himself.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji grew angrier still and, following a plan of Zhang Youxin and Li Xu, promoted Yu, Xifan, and Liu Qichu as remonstrance officials to watch for openings against Shen, while secretly allying with the eunuch Wang Shoucheng.

sentences.zh: 會敬宗立，逢吉知紳失勢可乘，使守澄從容奏言：「先帝始議立太子，杜元穎、李紳勸立深王，獨宰相逢吉請立陛下，而李續、李虞助之。

translations.literal: It happened that Emperor Jingzong took the throne; Fengji knew Shen had lost power and could be seized; he had Shoucheng at ease memorialize saying: "When the late emperor first deliberated establishing the heir, Du Yuanying and Li Shen urged establishing the Prince of Shen; only Chancellor Fengji asked to establish Your Majesty, while Li Xu and Li Yu assisted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong ascended the throne, Fengji saw that Shen had lost power and could be struck. He had Shoucheng calmly report to the throne, "When the late emperor first debated the succession, Du Yuanying and Li Shen urged naming the Prince of Shen. Only Chancellor Fengji asked that Your Majesty be named heir, with Li Xu and Li Yu supporting him.

sentences.zh: 」逢吉乘間言紳嘗不利於陛下，請逐之。

translations.literal: " Fengji seized the interval to say Shen had once been unfavorable to Your Majesty and asked to expel him.
translations.idiomatic: " Seizing the moment, Fengji added that Shen had once been hostile to the emperor and asked that he be driven away.

sentences.zh: 帝初即位，不能辨，乃貶紳為端州司馬。

translations.literal: The emperor had just taken the throne and could not distinguish; he then demoted Shen to Administrator of Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The new emperor could not tell truth from slander and demoted Shen to Administrator of Duan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 棲楚等怒得善地，皆切齒。

translations.literal: Qichu and others were angry he received a good place, all gnashing teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Qichu and his allies, furious that Shen had landed in so mild a place, gnashed their teeth.

sentences.zh: 詔下，百官賀逢吉，唯右拾遺吳思不往，逢吉斥思，令告大行喪於吐蕃。

translations.literal: When the edict descended, the hundred officials congratulated Fengji; only Right Remonstrance Official Wu Si did not go; Fengji expelled Si and ordered him to announce the Grand Mourning in Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When the edict was issued the officials congratulated Fengji—only Right Remonstrance Official Wu Si refused to attend. Fengji banished Si, ordering him to announce the grand mourning in Tibet.

sentences.zh: 此時，人無敢言者，惟韋處厚屢言紳枉，折逢吉之奸。

translations.literal: At this time no one dared speak; only Wei Chuhou repeatedly said Shen was wronged and broke Fengji's treachery.
translations.idiomatic: At that time no one dared speak up except Wei Chuhou, who repeatedly declared Shen's innocence and exposed Fengji's treachery.

sentences.zh: 後天子於禁中得先帝手緘書一笥，發之，見裴度、元穎、紳三疏請立帝為嗣，始大感悟，悉焚逢吉黨所上謗書。

translations.literal: Later the Son of Heaven in the forbidden precinct obtained one case of the late emperor's hand-sealed writings; opening it, he saw three memorials of Pei Du, Yuan Ying, and Shen requesting to establish the emperor as heir; he then greatly awakened in understanding and burned all the slanderous writings submitted by Fengji's faction.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in the inner palace, the emperor found a case of his father's sealed writings. Opening it, he discovered three memorials by Pei Du, Yuan Ying, and Shen asking that he be named heir. He was deeply moved and burned every slanderous document Fengji's faction had submitted.

sentences.zh: 始，紳南逐，歷封、康間，湍瀨險澀，惟乘漲流乃濟。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Shen was driven south; passing between Feng and Kang, rapids and shoals were dangerous and sluggish; only riding the swollen current could one cross.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen was first banished south he traveled between Feng and Kang, where rapids and shoals were treacherous and could be crossed only when the current ran high.

sentences.zh: 康州有媼龍祠，舊傳能致雲雨，紳以書禱，俄而大漲。

translations.literal: Kang Prefecture had the Old Dragon Mother's shrine; by old tradition it could bring clouds and rain; Shen with a written prayer prayed, and soon the waters greatly rose.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Prefecture had a shrine to the Dragon Mother, said since old times to summon rain. Shen prayed there in writing, and soon the river swelled greatly.

sentences.zh: 寶歷赦令不言左降官與量移，處厚執爭，詔為追定，得徙江州長史，遷滁、壽二州刺史。

translations.literal: The Baoli amnesty edict did not speak of demoted officials and measured transfers; Chuhou firmly contended; an edict was made to fix it retroactively; he was able to transfer to Administrator of Jiang Prefecture, then moved to Prefect of Chu and Shou.
translations.idiomatic: The Baoli amnesty did not mention demoted officials eligible for transfer. Chuhou argued the point firmly until an edict was issued to correct the omission, allowing Shen to move to Administrator of Jiang Prefecture and later to serve as Prefect of Chu and Shou.

sentences.zh: 霍山多虎，擷茶者病之，治機阱，發民跡射，不能止。

translations.literal: Huoshan had many tigers; tea pickers were afflicted by them; they set mechanical traps and mobilized the people to track and shoot, but could not stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Huo teemed with tigers that plagued the tea pickers. Traps were set and locals organized to track and shoot them, yet the attacks did not cease.

sentences.zh: 紳至，盡去之，虎不為暴。

translations.literal: When Shen arrived, he completely removed them; tigers did not act violently.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen arrived he had all the traps removed, and the tigers ceased their depredations.

sentences.zh: 以太子賓客分司東都。

translations.literal: He was made Honored Guest of the Heir Apparent with separate service at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Honored Guest of the Heir Apparent with nominal duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 太和中，李德裕當國，擢紳浙東觀察使。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era Li Deyu held the state and promoted Shen to Military Commissioner of Zhedong.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era, when Li Deyu held power, Shen was promoted to Military Commissioner of Zhedong.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔方得君，復以太子賓客分司。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin had just gained the ruler and again made him Honored Guest of the Heir Apparent with separate service.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zongmin gained the emperor's ear, Shen was again reduced to Honored Guest of the Heir Apparent with nominal duty.

sentences.zh: 開成初，鄭覃以紳為河南尹。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng, Zheng Tan made Shen Metropolitan Governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng era Zheng Tan appointed him Metropolitan Governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 河南多惡少，或危帽散衣，擊大毯，屍官道，車馬不敢前。

translations.literal: Henan had many rowdies; some wore tall hats and loose clothes, striking large balls and lying corpse-like across the official road so that horses and carriages dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Henan teemed with hoodlums. Some wore tall hats and disheveled dress, beating large balls and sprawling across the highway until traffic dared not pass.

sentences.zh: 紳治剛嚴，皆望風遁去。

translations.literal: Shen governed with stern rigor, and all fled at the mere sight of him.
translations.idiomatic: Shen governed with stern rigor, and they all fled at the mere report of him.

sentences.zh: 遷宣武節度使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Commissioner of Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Military Commissioner of Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 大旱，蝗不入境。

translations.literal: During a great drought, locusts did not enter his territory.
translations.idiomatic: During a severe drought, locusts did not cross into his circuit.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，徙淮南，召拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，進尚書右仆射、門下侍郎，封趙郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong took the throne, Shen was moved to Huainan, then summoned as Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Minister of the Chancellery, and enfeoffed as Duke of Zhao Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzong ascended the throne, Shen was transferred to Huainan, then recalled as Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor, promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and Vice Minister of the Chancellery, and enfeoffed Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 居位四年，以足緩不任朝謁，辭位，以檢校右仆射平章事，復節度淮南。

translations.literal: After four years in office, because his feet were slow and he could not attend court audiences, he resigned his post and served as Acting Right Vice Director and Grand Councillor while again commanding Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He held office four years, then pleaded that his feet were too weak for court attendance, resigned the chief post, and served as Acting Right Vice Director and Grand Councillor while returning to command Huainan.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太尉，謚文肅。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Grand Marshal, with the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously honored as Grand Marshal with the posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 始，灃人吳汝納者，韶州刺史武陵兄子也。

translations.literal: At the beginning, one Wu Runa of Feng was the nephew of Wuling, Prefect of Shao.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset there was Wu Runa of Feng, nephew of Wu Ling, Prefect of Shao.

sentences.zh: 武陵坐贓貶潘州司戶參軍死，汝納家被逐，久不調。

translations.literal: Wuling was convicted of corruption, demoted to Army Administrator of Pan Prefecture, and died; Runa's family was driven out and he long went without appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ling was convicted of corruption, demoted to army administrator of Pan Prefecture, and died. Runa's family was expelled and he long remained without office.

sentences.zh: 時李吉甫任宰相，汝納怨之，後遂附宗閔黨中。

translations.literal: At the time Li Jifu served as chancellor; Runa resented him and later attached himself to Li Zongmin's faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Jifu was chancellor, Runa bore a grudge against him and later joined Li Zongmin's faction.

sentences.zh: 會昌時，為永寧尉，弟湘為江都尉。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he was made Commandant of Yongning; his younger brother Xiang was Commandant of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: During Huichang he served as commandant of Yongning; his younger brother Wu Xiang was commandant of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 部人訟湘受贓狼籍，身娶民顏悅女。

translations.literal: District people sued Xiang for corruption in heaps and for personally marrying a commoner's daughter, Yan Yue's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Locals accused Xiang of rampant corruption and of taking a commoner's daughter, Yan Yue's daughter, as his wife.

sentences.zh: 紳使觀察判官魏铏鞫湘，罪明白，論報殺之。

translations.literal: Shen had Observation Commissioner Wei Tong interrogate Xiang; the crime was clear and he was sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had the observation commission's judge Wei Tong try Xiang. The guilt was clear and Xiang was sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 時，議者謂吳氏世與宰相有嫌，疑紳內顧望，織成其罪。

translations.literal: At the time commentators said the Wu clan for generations had grudges with chancellors and suspected Shen of inward partiality, weaving his guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators said the Wu family had long feuded with chancellors and suspected Shen of partiality in fabricating the case.

sentences.zh: 諫官屢論列，詔遣御史崔元藻覆按，元藻言湘盜用程糧錢有狀，娶部人女不實，按悅嘗為青州衙推，而妻王故衣冠女，不應坐。

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials repeatedly memorialized; an edict sent Censor Cui Yuanyao to reinvestigate. Yuanyao said Xiang had indeed embezzled transport grain funds, that marrying a district woman's daughter was not true, and that Yan Yue had once been a Qingzhou yamen aide while his wife Wang was a woman of an old gentry family and should not be implicated.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials repeatedly protested until an edict sent Censor Cui Yuanyao to reinvestigate. Yuanyao reported that Xiang had indeed embezzled transport funds, that the charge of marrying a local woman was false, and that Yan Yue had been a Qingzhou yamen aide while his wife Wang came from an old gentry family and should not be punished.

sentences.zh: 德裕惡元藻持兩端，奏貶崖州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: Deyu detested Yuanyao's fence-sitting and memorialized to demote him to Army Administrator of Ya Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu hated Yuanyao's wavering and had him demoted to army administrator of Ya Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，德裕去位，紳已卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne, Deyu left office and Shen had already died.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne, Deyu fell from power and Shen was already dead.

sentences.zh: 崔鉉等久不得誌，導汝納使為湘訟，言：「湘素直，為人誣蔑，大校重牢，五木被體，吏至以娶妻資媵結贓。

translations.literal: Cui Xuan and others had long been unable to satisfy their ambition and guided Runa to sue on Xiang's behalf, saying: "Xiang was by nature upright, was slandered by others, was put in heavy fetters in a major prison, had the five punishments applied to his body, and officials even fabricated corruption by treating his marriage portion and concubine price as bribes."
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan and others, long thwarted in their designs, coached Runa to sue for Xiang, claiming Xiang was upright, had been slandered, was shackled in a major prison and subjected to the five punishments, while officials fabricated bribery from his bride-price and dowry.

sentences.zh: 」且言：「顏悅故士族，湘罪皆不當死，紳枉殺之。

translations.literal: " Moreover they said: "Yan Yue was of an old gentry house; none of Xiang's crimes warranted death; Shen wrongly killed him."
translations.idiomatic: " They added that Yan Yue was of an old gentry house, that none of Xiang's offenses warranted death, and that Shen had killed him unjustly.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「湘死，紳令即瘞，不得歸葬。

translations.literal: " They also said: "When Xiang died, Shen ordered immediate burial and would not allow return for funeral rites."
translations.idiomatic: " They also said that when Xiang died Shen ordered immediate burial and would not permit his body to be returned home.

sentences.zh: 按紳以舊宰相鎮一方，恣威權。

translations.literal: According to Shen, as a former chancellor commanding a region, he wielded power willfully.
translations.idiomatic: They charged that Shen, a former chancellor ruling a circuit, had wielded power willfully.

sentences.zh: 凡戮有罪，猶待秋分；

translations.literal: Even when executing the guilty one still waited for the autumn equinox;
translations.idiomatic: Even when executing the guilty he still waited for the autumn equinox;

sentences.zh: 湘無辜，盛夏被殺。

translations.literal: Xiang was innocent yet was killed in midsummer.
translations.idiomatic: yet Xiang, though innocent, was killed in midsummer.

sentences.zh: 」崔元藻銜德裕斥己，即翻其辭，因言：「御史覆獄還，皆對天子別白是非，德裕權軋天下，使不得對，具獄不付有司，但用紳奏而寘湘死。

translations.literal: " Cui Yuanyao, resenting Deyu's dismissal of him, then reversed his testimony and said: "When censors return from reinvestigating cases they all explain right and wrong separately to the Son of Heaven; Deyu's power crushed the realm and prevented them from speaking; the full dossier was not given to the responsible offices but only Shen's memorial was used to put Xiang to death."
translations.idiomatic: " Cui Yuanyao, nursing resentment at Deyu's dismissal, reversed his testimony and said censors returning from reinvestigation should explain verdicts to the throne, but Deyu's power had crushed the realm, prevented such audiences, withheld the full dossier from the courts, and relied solely on Shen's memorial to kill Xiang.

sentences.zh: 」是時，德裕已失權，而宗閔故黨令狐、崔鉉、白敏中皆當路，因是逞憾，以利誘動元藻等，使三司結紳杖鉞作藩，虐殺良平，準神龍詔書，酷吏歿者官爵皆奪，子孫不得進宦，紳雖亡，請從《春秋》戮死者之比。

translations.literal: " At that time Deyu had already lost power, but Li Zongmin's old partisans Linghu, Cui Xuan, and Bai Minzhong all held the road; they therefore vented their rancor, enticing Yuanyao and others with profit, and had the Three Offices conclude that Shen, wielding authority as a frontier commander, cruelly killed the innocent and the peaceful; according to the Shenlong edict, dead cruel officials should have offices and titles stripped and descendants barred from office; though Shen was dead, they asked to apply the Spring and Autumn analogy for punishing the dead.
translations.idiomatic: " Deyu had already fallen, but Zongmin's old allies Linghu, Cui Xuan, and Bai Minzhong held power. Venting old rancor, they bribed Yuanyao and others until the Three Offices ruled that Shen, as a regional commander, had cruelly killed the innocent. Citing the Shenlong edict on dead cruel officials, they stripped three ranks from Shen and barred his descendants from office, invoking the Spring and Autumn precedent for punishing the dead.

sentences.zh: 詔削紳三官，子孫不得仕。

translations.literal: An edict stripped Shen of three offices and barred his descendants from serving.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped three ranks from Shen and barred his descendants from office.

sentences.zh: 貶德裕等，擢汝納左拾遺，元藻武功令。

translations.literal: Deyu and others were demoted; Runa was promoted to Left Remonstrance Official and Yuanyao made magistrate of Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu and others were demoted, Runa was promoted to Left Remonstrance Official, and Yuanyao was made magistrate of Wugong.

sentences.zh: 始，紳以文藝節操見用，而屢為怨仇所拫卻，卒能自伸其才，以名位終。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Shen was employed for literary talent and integrity, yet repeatedly was struck down by resentful enemies, and in the end was able to extend his talent and end in fame and position.
translations.idiomatic: Shen had risen on literary talent and integrity, was repeatedly struck down by enemies, yet in the end extended his talents and finished in high office.

sentences.zh: 所至務為威烈，或陷暴刻，故雖沒而坐湘冤雲。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he strove for stern authority, sometimes falling into harsh severity; therefore even after death the injustice of Xiang's case remained.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he pursued stern authority and sometimes harsh severity; hence even after death the injustice of Xiang's case lingered.

sentences.zh: 李讓夷，字達心，系本隴西。

translations.literal: Li Rangyi, styled Daxin, traced his lineage to Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Rangyi, courtesy name Daxin, was of Longxi descent.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，辟鎮國李絳府判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was recruited as judge in Li Jiang's Zhenguo headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and entered Li Jiang's Zhenguo headquarters as a judge.

sentences.zh: 又從西川杜元穎幕府。

translations.literal: He also followed Du Yuanying's western Sichuan staff.
translations.idiomatic: He later served on Du Yuanying's staff in western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 與宋申錫善，申錫為翰林學士，薦讓夷右拾遺，俄召拜學士。

translations.literal: He was friendly with Song Shenxi; when Shenxi became a Hanlin academician he recommended Rangyi as Right Remonstrance Official, and soon he was summoned as an academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was close to Song Shenxi. When Shenxi entered the Hanlin Academy he recommended Rangyi as Right Remonstrance Official, and Rangyi was soon summoned as an academician.

sentences.zh: 素善薛廷老，廷老不飭細檢，數飲酒不治職，罷去，坐是亦奪職。

translations.literal: He had long been friendly with Xue Tinglao; Tinglao did not discipline minor conduct, repeatedly drank wine and neglected duty, was dismissed, and for this Rangyi also lost his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was also close to Xue Tinglao. Tinglao was careless and often drunk on duty; when Tinglao was dismissed Rangyi lost his post as well.

sentences.zh: 累進諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Remonstrance Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Remonstrance Grandee.

sentences.zh: 開成初，起居舍人李褒免，文宗謂李石曰：「褚遂良以諫議大夫兼起居郎，今諫議誰歟？

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaicheng, Attendant of the Heir Apparent Li Bao was dismissed. Emperor Wenzong said to Li Shi: "Chu Suiliang once combined Remonstrance Grandee with Attendant of the Heir Apparent—who holds remonstrance now?
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaicheng, when Attendant of the Heir Apparent Li Bao was removed, Wenzong asked Li Shi, "Chu Suiliang once combined remonstrance grandee with heir-apparent attendant—who holds that remonstrance post now?

sentences.zh: 可言其人。

translations.literal: One may speak of the man for it."
translations.idiomatic: Name someone fit for it."

sentences.zh: 」石以馮定、孫簡、蕭俶、李讓夷對，帝曰：「讓夷可也。

translations.literal: " Shi named Feng Ding, Sun Jian, Xiao Ju, and Li Rangyi; the emperor said: "Rangyi will do."
translations.idiomatic: " Shi named Feng Ding, Sun Jian, Xiao Ju, and Li Rangyi. The emperor said, "Rangyi will do."

sentences.zh: 」李固言請用崔球、張次宗。

translations.literal: " Li Guyuan asked to use Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Guyuan urged Cui Qiu and Zhang Cizong.

sentences.zh: 鄭覃曰：「球故與李宗閔善，且記註操筆在赤墀下，所書為後世法，不可用黨人。

translations.literal: " Zheng Tan said: "Qiu was formerly friendly with Li Zongmin, and moreover the record-keeper's brush below the red steps becomes a model for later ages—one cannot use a partisan.
translations.idiomatic: " Zheng Tan said, "Qiu was once close to Li Zongmin, and the court recorder's brush below the red steps becomes a model for posterity—a partisan must not hold it.

sentences.zh: 若裴中孺、李讓夷，臣不敢有言。

translations.literal: " If it is Pei Zhongru or Li Rangyi, your subject dares not speak further."
translations.idiomatic: As for Pei Zhongru or Li Rangyi, I have nothing to say against them."

sentences.zh: 」乃決用讓夷，進中書舍人。

translations.literal: " They then decided on Rangyi and promoted him to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: " Rangyi was appointed and promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 既而李玨、楊嗣復以覃之薦，終帝世不得遷。

translations.literal: " Thereafter Li Jue and Yang Sifu, because of Tan's recommendation, blocked his advancement for the rest of the emperor's reign.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter Li Jue and Yang Sifu, resenting Tan's recommendation, blocked his advancement for the rest of Wenzong's reign.

sentences.zh: 武宗初，李德裕復入，三遷至尚書右丞，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuzong's reign Li Deyu returned to power, was thrice promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and appointed Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Early under Wuzong, Li Deyu returned to court, rose thrice to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, and became Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 潞州平，檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: When Luzhou was pacified he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Luzhou was pacified he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 宣宗立，進司空、門下侍郎，為大行山陵使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong took the throne he was advanced to Minister of Works and Vice Minister of the Chancellery and made commissioner for the imperial tomb of the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong ascended the throne he was promoted to Minister of Works and Vice Minister of the Chancellery and made commissioner for the late emperor's tomb.

sentences.zh: 未復土，拜淮南節度使。

translations.literal: Before the earth was returned he was appointed Military Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Before the mourning earth was restored he was appointed Military Commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 以疾願還，卒於道，贈司徒。

translations.literal: Pleading illness he wished to return and died on the road; he was posthumously made Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded illness to return, died on the road, and was posthumously made Minister of Education.

sentences.zh: 讓夷廉介不妄交，位雖顯劇，以儉約自將，為世咨美。

translations.literal: Rangyi was incorrupt and did not associate rashly; though his position was eminent and taxing, he restrained himself by frugality and was praised by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Rangyi was incorruptible and cautious in friendship. Though his posts were weighty, he lived frugally and was praised by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 曹確，字剛中，河南河南人。

translations.literal: Cao Que, styled Gangzhong, was a man of Henan in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Que, courtesy name Gangzhong, was from Henan in the Henan region.

sentences.zh: 擢進士第，歷踐中外官，累拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, served through central and local offices, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination, served in central and local posts, and rose to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 懿宗咸通中，以本官同中書門下平章事，俄進中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era of Emperor Yizong he became Associate Grand Councillor with his existing office and soon advanced to Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yizong in the Xiantong era he became Associate Grand Councillor in his existing post and soon Vice Minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 確邃儒術，器識方重，動循法度。

translations.literal: Que was steeped in Confucian learning, his capacity and judgment square and weighty, and his actions followed law and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Que was steeped in Confucian learning, upright in judgment, and measured in conduct.

sentences.zh: 時帝薄於德，昵寵優人李可及。

translations.literal: The emperor at the time was thin in virtue and doted on the actor Li Keji.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was weak in virtue and doted on the actor Li Keji.

sentences.zh: 可及者，能新聲，自度曲，辭調悽折，京師俞薄少年爭慕之，號為「拍彈」。

translations.literal: Keji could produce new sounds, composed his own tunes, and his lyrics were plaintively broken; the frivolous youths of the capital all admired him and called it 'patting and strumming.'
translations.idiomatic: Keji invented new music, composed his own tunes with plaintive lyrics, and frivolous youths of the capital admired him under the name 'patting and strumming.'

sentences.zh: 同昌公主喪畢，帝與郭淑妃悼念不已，可及為帝造曲，曰《嘆百年》，教舞者數百，皆珠翠襐飾，刻畫魚龍地衣，度用繒五千，倚曲作辭，哀思裴回，聞者皆涕下。

translations.literal: When Princess Tongchang's mourning ended the emperor and Consort Guo could not cease grieving. Keji composed for the emperor a piece called 'Lament for a Century,' taught several hundred dancers all adorned in pearls and kingfisher feathers, with carpets carved in fish and dragon designs, using five thousand bolts of silk; relying on the tune he wrote lyrics of circling sorrow so that hearers all wept.
translations.idiomatic: After Princess Tongchang's mourning ended the emperor and Consort Guo still grieved. Keji composed 'Lament for a Century' for him, trained hundreds of dancers in pearls and kingfisher trim on carpets carved with fish and dragons, using five thousand bolts of silk; the lyrics were so mournful that listeners wept.

sentences.zh: 舞闋，珠寶覆地，帝以為天下之至悲，愈寵之。

translations.literal: When the dance ended pearls and jewels covered the ground; the emperor thought it the greatest sorrow under heaven and favored him still more.
translations.idiomatic: When the dance ended jewels carpeted the ground. The emperor called it the world's supreme sorrow and favored Keji all the more.

sentences.zh: 家嘗娶婦，帝曰：「第去，吾當賜酒。

translations.literal: When his household once took a bride the emperor said: "Just go—I shall bestow wine."
translations.idiomatic: When his household took a bride the emperor said, "Go home—I shall send wine."

sentences.zh: 」俄而使者負二銀珰與之，皆珠珍也。

translations.literal: " Soon envoys carried two silver pendants to him, all filled with pearls and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: " Envoys soon arrived bearing two silver pendants filled with pearls and gems.

sentences.zh: 可及憑恩橫甚，人無敢斥，遂擢為威衛將軍。

translations.literal: Keji relied on favor and was extremely overbearing; no one dared reprove him, and he was promoted to General of the Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Keji grew insolent on imperial favor; none dared reprove him, and he was made a general of the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 確曰：「太宗著令，文武官六百四十三，謂房玄齡曰：『朕設此待天下賢士。

translations.literal: Que said: "Taizong issued an ordinance of six hundred forty-three civil and military offices and told Fang Xuanling: 'I established these to await worthy men under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Que said, "Taizong fixed six hundred forty-three civil and military posts and told Fang Xuanling, 'I established these to await worthy men under heaven.

sentences.zh: 工商雜流，假使技出等夷，正當厚給以財，不可假以官，與賢者比肩立、同坐食也。

translations.literal: " For merchants, artisans, and miscellaneous classes, even if their skill surpassed their peers, they should rightly be richly supplied with wealth and must not be lent office to stand shoulder to shoulder and eat together with the worthy."
translations.idiomatic: Merchants and artisans, even if skilled beyond their peers, should receive wealth, not office to stand and dine beside the worthy."

sentences.zh: 』文宗欲以樂工尉遲璋為王府率，拾遺竇洵直固爭，卒授光州長史。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wenzong wished to make the musician Yuchi Zhang Commandant of the Princely Household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi firmly contended and in the end he was given Administrator of Guang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzong wished to make the musician Yuchi Zhang commandant of the princely household; Remonstrance Official Dou Xunzhi protested until Yuchi was made administrator of Guang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 今而位將軍，不可。

translations.literal: " Now to make him a general is not permissible."
translations.idiomatic: To make Keji a general now is impermissible."

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 至僖宗立，始貶死。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong took the throne he was at last demoted and died.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Xizong ascended the throne was Keji demoted and died.

sentences.zh: 方幸時，惟確屢言之。

translations.literal: While favor lasted, only Que repeatedly spoke against it.
translations.idiomatic: While favor lasted, only Que spoke against it repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 而神策中尉西門季玄者，亦剛鯁，謂可及曰：「汝以巧佞惑天子，當族滅！

translations.literal: The Shence Army Commandant Ximen Jixuan was also stern and upright and said to Keji: "You use clever flattery to bewitch the Son of Heaven—you should be exterminated to the clan!"
translations.idiomatic: Shence commandant Ximen Jixuan was likewise stern and told Keji, "You bewitch the Son of Heaven with clever flattery—your clan should be exterminated!"

sentences.zh: 」嘗見其受賜，謂曰：「今載以官車，後籍沒亦當爾。」

translations.literal: " Once seeing him receive gifts he said: "Today it is carried on an official cart; later when property is confiscated it will be the same."
translations.idiomatic: Seeing him receive gifts, Jixuan said, "Today it rides on an official cart; when your property is confiscated it will be the same."

sentences.zh: 確居位六年，進尚書右仆射，以同平章事出為鎮海節度使，徙河中，卒。

translations.literal: After six years in office Que advanced to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, left as Grand Councillor to become Military Commissioner of Zhenhai, was moved to Hedong, and died.
translations.idiomatic: After six years Que became Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, left court as grand councillor to command Zhenhai, was transferred to Hedong, and died.

sentences.zh: 始，畢諴與確同宰相，俱有雅望，世謂「曹畢」雲。

translations.literal: At the beginning Bi Xian and Que were chancellors together, both with elegant reputation; the age called them 'Cao and Bi.'
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Bi Xian and Que had served together as chancellors with fine reputations; people called them 'Cao and Bi.'

sentences.zh: 弟汾，以忠武軍節度使入為戶部侍郎，判度支，卒。

translations.literal: His younger brother Fen entered as Vice Minister of Revenue and Commissioner of Finance from Military Commissioner of Zhongwu and died.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Fen came to court as Vice Minister of Revenue and finance commissioner from Military Commissioner of Zhongwu and died.

sentences.zh: 劉瞻，字幾之，其先出彭城，後徙桂陽。

translations.literal: Liu Zhan, styled Jizhi, his ancestors came out of Pengcheng and later moved to Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhan, courtesy name Jizhi, was descended from Pengcheng and later moved to Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 舉進士、博學宏詞，皆中。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and the erudite examinations in expansive learning and both succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He passed both the jinshi and the erudite examinations in expansive learning.

sentences.zh: 徐商辟署鹽鐵府，累遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Xu Shang recruited him to the Salt and Iron Commission and he was repeatedly promoted to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Shang recruited him to the Salt and Iron Commission; he rose to Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 劉彖執政，薦為翰林學士，拜中書舍人，進承旨。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhan held power he recommended him as Hanlin academician, appointed Secretariat Drafter, and advanced him to Chief Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhan held power he recommended Zhan as Hanlin academician, made him Secretariat Drafter, and advanced him to Chief Drafter.

sentences.zh: 出為河東節度使。

translations.literal: He went out as Military Commissioner of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Military Commissioner of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 咸通十一年，以中書侍郎同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Xiantong he became Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In 870 he became Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 同昌公主薨，懿宗捕太醫韓紹宗等送詔獄，逮系宗族數百人。

translations.literal: When Princess Tongchang died Emperor Yizong arrested the imperial physicians Han Shaozong and others and sent them to the edict prison, seizing several hundred clansmen.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Tongchang died Yizong arrested imperial physician Han Shaozong and others, sent them to the edict prison, and seized hundreds of their clansmen.

sentences.zh: 瞻喻諫官，皆依違無敢言，即自上疏固爭：「紹宗窮其術不能效，情有可矜。

translations.literal: Zhan instructed the remonstrance officials, but all wavered and none dared speak; he then himself submitted a firm memorial: "Shaozong exhausted his arts without effect—there is reason for pity.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan urged the remonstrance officials, but all hedged. He then memorialized firmly, "Shaozong exhausted his arts without success—he deserves pity.

sentences.zh: 陛下徇愛女，囚平民，忿不顧難，取肆暴不明之謗。

translations.literal: " Your Majesty indulges love for a daughter, imprisons common people, vents anger without regard for difficulty, and invites the slander of wanton violence and unclear judgment."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty indulges love for a daughter, imprisons commoners, vents rage heedlessly, and invites slander for arbitrary cruelty."

sentences.zh: 」帝大怒，即日賜罷，以檢校刑部尚書、同平章事為荊南節度使。

translations.literal: " The emperor was greatly angered and that same day bestowed dismissal; he was made Acting Minister of Punishments and Grand Councillor and Military Commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and dismissed him the same day, appointing him Acting Minister of Punishments, Grand Councillor, and Military Commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 路巖、韋保衡從為惡言聞帝，俄斥廉州刺史。

translations.literal: Lu Yan and Wei Baoheng followed with malicious words heard by the emperor, and soon he was expelled as Prefect of Lian.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yan and Wei Baoheng whispered slanders to the emperor, and soon Zhan was demoted to Prefect of Lian.

sentences.zh: 於是，翰林學士鄭畋以責詔不深切，御史中丞孫皇、諫議大夫高湘等坐與瞻善，分貶嶺南。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Hanlin Academician Zheng Tian was punished because the reprimand edict was not deep enough; Vice Censor-in-Chief Sun Huang, Remonstrance Grandee Gao Xiang, and others were punished for friendship with Zhan and were separately demoted to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Zheng Tian was punished because the reprimand edict was too mild. Vice Censor-in-Chief Sun Huang, Remonstrance Grandee Gao Xiang, and others were demoted to Lingnan for friendship with Zhan.

sentences.zh: 巖等殊未慊，按圖視州道萬里，即貶州司戶參軍事，命李庾作詔極詆，將遂殺之。

translations.literal: Yan and the others were still not satisfied; consulting maps they saw the prefecture was ten thousand li distant and at once demoted him to Army Administrator of the prefecture, ordered Li Yu to draft an edict of extreme slander, and were about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan and his allies were still unsatisfied. Seeing on the map that the post lay ten thousand li away, they demoted Zhan to army administrator of the prefecture, had Li Yu draft a savage edict, and were about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 天下謂瞻鯁正，特為讒擠，舉以為冤。

translations.literal: All under heaven said Zhan was upright and had been specially squeezed out by slander; everyone regarded it as injustice.
translations.idiomatic: The realm held that Zhan was upright and had been squeezed out by slander; all deemed it injustice.

sentences.zh: 幽州節度使張公素上疏申解，巖等不敢害。

translations.literal: Military Commissioner Zhang Gongsu of You submitted a memorial in his defense; Yan and the others did not dare harm him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gongsu, Military Commissioner of You, memorialized in his defense; Yan and the others did not dare harm him.

sentences.zh: 僖宗立，徙康、虢二州刺史，以刑部尚書召，復以中書侍郎平章事，居位三月卒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong took the throne Zhan was moved to Prefect of Kang and Guo, recalled as Minister of Punishments, and again made Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor; after three months in office he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong ascended the throne Zhan was moved to Kang and Guo, recalled as Minister of Punishments, again made Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Grand Councillor, and died after three months.

sentences.zh: 瞻為人廉約，所得俸以余濟親舊之窶困者，家不留儲。

translations.literal: Zhan as a man was frugal; he used surplus salary to aid poor relatives and old friends and kept no stores at home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was frugal, using surplus salary to aid poor kin and friends and keeping no stores at home.

sentences.zh: 無第舍，四方獻饋不及門，行己終始完潔。

translations.literal: He had no mansion; gifts from the four directions did not reach his gate; his conduct from beginning to end was whole and pure.
translations.idiomatic: He owned no mansion; gifts never reached his door; his conduct remained pure start to finish.

sentences.zh: 弟助，字元德，性仁孝，幼時與諸兄遊，至食飲，取最下者。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhu, styled Yuande, was by nature filial; when young he played with his elder brothers, at food and drink he took the lowest portion.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhu, courtesy name Yuande, was filial. As a boy playing with his elder brothers he always took the lowest portion at meals.

sentences.zh: 及長，能文辭，喜黃老言。

translations.literal: When grown he could write literary compositions and delighted in Yellow Emperor and Laozi teachings.
translations.idiomatic: Grown, he could write well and delighted in Daoist teachings.

sentences.zh: 年二十卒。

translations.literal: He died at twenty.
translations.idiomatic: He died at twenty.

sentences.zh: 李蔚，字茂休，系本隴西。

translations.literal: Li Wei, styled Maoxiu, traced his lineage to Longxi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Wei, courtesy name Maoxiu, was of Longxi descent.

sentences.zh: 舉進士、書判拔萃，皆中。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi and the selected writings examinations with distinction, both succeeding.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi and the distinguished writings examination.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史，擢累尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor and was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor and rose to Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 懿宗惑浮屠，常飯萬僧禁中，自為贊唄。

translations.literal: Emperor Yizong was deluded by Buddhism and regularly fed ten thousand monks in the palace, himself chanting praise hymns.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong was deluded by Buddhism and regularly fed ten thousand monks in the palace while chanting hymns himself.

sentences.zh: 蔚上疏切諫，引狄仁傑、姚元崇、辛替否所言，譏病時弊。

translations.literal: Wei submitted a sharp memorial of remonstrance, citing what Di Renjie, Yao Chong, and Xin Tifou had said, ridiculing the ailments of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Wei submitted a sharp memorial citing Di Renjie, Yao Chong, and Xin Tifou and ridiculing the age's failings.

sentences.zh: 帝不聽，但以虛禮褒答。

translations.literal: The emperor would not listen but only answered with empty courtesy and praise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not listen and answered only with empty courtesy.

sentences.zh: 俄拜京兆尹、太常卿。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Metropolitan Governor of Jingzhao and Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 出為宣武節度使，徙淮南。

translations.literal: He went out as Military Commissioner of Xuanwu and was moved to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Military Commissioner of Xuanwu, then transferred to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 代還，民詣闕請留，詔許一歲。

translations.literal: When replaced and returning, the people went to the gate to ask that he remain; an edict permitted one year.
translations.idiomatic: When his replacement arrived the people petitioned the throne to keep him; an edict allowed him one more year.

sentences.zh: 僖宗乾符初，以吏部尚書同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfu under Emperor Xizong he was made Minister of Civil Office and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianfu era under Xizong he became Minister of Civil Office and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 罷為東都留守。

translations.literal: He was dismissed as Defender of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed to serve as Defender of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 河東亂，殺其帥崔季康，用邠寧李侃代之，士不附，以蔚嘗在太原府有惠政，為人所懷，拜河東節度使，同平章事。

translations.literal: Hedong was in turmoil and killed its commander Cui Jikang; Binning's Li Kan was used to replace him; the soldiers did not attach themselves; because Wei had once had benevolent government in the Taiyuan office and was cherished by people, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Hedong and Associate Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong rebelled and killed its commander Cui Jikang. Li Kan of Binning was sent to replace him, but the troops would not accept him. Because Wei had once served in Taiyuan with benevolent rule and was still beloved, he was appointed Military Commissioner of Hedong and Associate Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 至鎮三日，卒。

translations.literal: Reaching the command three days, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He reached his post and died three days later.

sentences.zh: 始，懿宗成安國祠，賜寶坐二，度高二丈，構以沈檀，塗髹，鏤龍鳳葩蘤，金扣之，上施復坐，陳經幾其前，四隅立瑞鳥神人，高數尺，磴道以升，前被繡囊錦襜，珍麗精絕。

translations.literal: At the beginning Emperor Yizong completed the Chengan State shrine and bestowed two jeweled thrones, their height two zhang, constructed of heavy sandalwood, coated with lacquer, carved with dragon, phoenix, and floral patterns, fastened with gold, above which were set canopy seats; sutra tables were placed before them; at the four corners stood auspicious birds and divine figures several feet high; steps led up; before them hung embroidered bags and brocade curtains—rare and exquisite beyond compare.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yizong completed the Chengan State shrine and bestowed two jeweled thrones two zhang high, built of heavy sandalwood, lacquered and carved with dragons, phoenixes, and flowers, trimmed in gold, topped with canopy seats. Sutra tables stood before them; at the four corners rose auspicious birds and divine figures several feet tall, with steps leading up. Embroidered bags and brocade curtains hung before them—splendor without equal.

sentences.zh: 咸通十四年春，詔迎佛骨鳳翔，或言：「昔憲宗嘗為此，俄晏駕。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year of Xiantong an edict welcomed the Buddha's relic from Fengxiang; some said: "Formerly Emperor Xianzong once did this and soon passed away.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of 873 an edict ordered the Buddha's relic brought from Fengxiang. Some warned, "When Xianzong did this he soon died.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「使朕生見之，死無恨！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Let me see it in life and I shall die without regret!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "If I can see it while I live, I shall die without regret!

sentences.zh: 」乃以金銀為剎，珠玉為帳，孔鷸周飾之，小者尋丈，高至倍，刻檀為檐註，陛墄塗黃金，每一剎，數百人舉之。

translations.literal: " He then made reliquary towers of gold and silver, canopies of pearls and jade, adorned all around with kingfishers; the small ones were a xun in height, the tall ones twice that; sandalwood was carved for eaves and pillars; steps and ramps were coated in gold; for each tower several hundred men lifted it.
translations.idiomatic: " He had reliquary towers made of gold and silver, canopies of pearl and jade, trimmed with kingfisher feathers. The smaller towers stood a xun high, the larger twice that. Sandalwood eaves and pillars were carved, steps gilded, and each tower required hundreds of men to carry it.

sentences.zh: 香輿前後系道，綴珠瑟瑟幡蓋，殘彩以為幢節，費無貲限。

translations.literal: Incense chariots stretched along the road before and behind; pearl and jadeite banners and canopies were strung; leftover brocades served as pennants; expense had no reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Incense chariots lined the road for miles, hung with pearl and jadeite banners and canopies, pennants fashioned from leftover brocades—cost beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，至長安，彩觀夾路，其徒導衛。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer it reached Chang'an; colored pavilions lined the road and the monks guided and guarded it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month it reached Chang'an. Colored pavilions lined the road while monks guided the procession.

sentences.zh: 天子禦安福樓迎拜，至泣下。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven attended at Anfu Tower to welcome and bow, even to weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received it at Anfu Tower, bowing until he wept.

sentences.zh: 詔賜兩街僧金幣，京師耆老及見元和事者，悉厚賜之。

translations.literal: An edict bestowed gold and coins on the monks of both monastic precincts; the elders of the capital and all who had witnessed Yuanhe affairs were all richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rewarded monks of both precincts with gold and cash, and richly compensated every elder in the capital who had lived through the Yuanhe era.

sentences.zh: 不逞小人至斷臂指，流血滿道。

translations.literal: Unruly petty men even cut off arms and fingers; blood flowed filling the road.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate men even cut off their own arms and fingers until blood filled the streets.

sentences.zh: 所過鄉聚，皆裒土為剎，相望於塗，爭以金翠抆飾。

translations.literal: Every village and hamlet passed was piled with earth for reliquary towers, gazing at one another along the road, competing to adorn them with gold and kingfisher green.
translations.idiomatic: Every village along the route piled earth into reliquary towers that faced one another along the road, each competing to adorn them with gold and kingfisher trim.

sentences.zh: 傳言剎悉震搖，若有光景雲。

translations.literal: Rumor said the towers all trembled and shook as if there were light, scenery, and clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Rumor held that the towers trembled and glowed as if wreathed in light and cloud.

sentences.zh: 京師高貲相與集大衢，作繒臺縵闕，註水銀為池，金玉為樹木，聚桑門羅像，考鼓鳴螺繼日夜。

translations.literal: The wealthy of the capital together gathered on the great avenues, made brocade platforms and curtained towers, poured mercury for pools, gold and jade for trees, assembled monks and arranged images, beating drums and sounding conchs day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy families of the capital gathered on the main avenues, erecting brocade platforms and curtained towers, pouring mercury into pools, fashioning trees of gold and jade, assembling monks and images, beating drums and sounding conchs day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 錦車繡輿，載歌舞從之。

translations.literal: Brocade carts and embroidered palanquins carried song and dance following it.
translations.idiomatic: Brocade carts and embroidered palanquins followed with singers and dancers.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，帝崩。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the emperor died.

sentences.zh: 方人主甘心篤向，如蔚言者甚多，皆不能救。

translations.literal: Just as the ruler willingly devoted himself, many like what Wei said could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Just as the ruler had willingly thrown himself into devotion, many who spoke as Wei had could not save him.

sentences.zh: 僖宗立，詔歸其骨，都人耆耋辭餞，或嗚咽流涕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xizong took the throne an edict returned the relic; the aged of the capital bid farewell at parting, some sobbing with flowing tears.
translations.idiomatic: When Xizong ascended the throne an edict sent the relic back. The aged of the capital came to bid it farewell, many weeping aloud.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：人之惑怪神也，甚哉！

translations.literal: The commentator says: How greatly people are deluded by strange spirits!
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: How deeply people are deluded by the supernatural!

sentences.zh: 若佛者，特西域一槁人耳。

translations.literal: As for the Buddha, he was merely a withered man of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha was nothing more than a gaunt man from the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 裸顛露足，以乞食自資，臒辱其身，屏營山樊，行一概之苦，本無求於人，徒屬稍稍從之。

translations.literal: Bareheaded with feet exposed, he supported himself by begging food, emaciated and humbling his body, secluded in mountain thickets, practicing uniform hardship, originally without seeking from others—only gradually did followers come after him.
translations.idiomatic: Bareheaded, feet exposed, he lived by begging, emaciating and humbling himself in mountain seclusion, practicing uniform austerity without asking anything of others—only slowly did followers gather.

sentences.zh: 然其言荒茫漫靡，夷幻變現，善推不驗無實之事，以鬼神死生貫為一條，據之不疑。

translations.literal: Yet his words were vast, vague, and diffuse, leveling illusions and transformations; he was skilled at inferring unverified and unreal matters, threading ghosts, spirits, death, and life into one strand, and holding it without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his teachings were vast and vague, leveling illusions and transformations, skilled at inferring what cannot be verified, threading ghosts, spirits, death, and life into one chain—and holding it without doubt.

sentences.zh: 掊嗜欲，棄親屬，大抵與黃老相出入。

translations.literal: He rejected desires and abandoned kin; in general he largely corresponded with Yellow Emperor and Laozi teachings.
translations.idiomatic: He rejected desire and abandoned kin, doctrines that largely overlap with the teachings of the Yellow Emperor and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 至漢十四葉，書入中國。

translations.literal: Reaching the fourteenth generation of Han, the texts entered China.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the fourteenth generation of Han did the texts enter China.

sentences.zh: 跡夫生人之情，以耳目不際為奇，以不可知為神，以物理之外為畏，以變化無方為聖，以生而死、死復生、回復償報、歆艷其間為或然，以賤近貴遠為。
