translations.literal: Tracing the feelings of living men: they take what eyes and ears do not reach as marvel; what cannot be known as divine; what lies beyond physical principle as fearful; unbounded transformation as sagehood; life turning to death, death returning to life, cyclic repayment and recompense, delighting in between as perhaps so; they treat what is near as base and what is far as noble.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing human nature: what eyes and ears cannot reach seems marvelous; what cannot be known seems divine; what lies beyond physical law seems fearful; unbounded change seems holy; life into death, death into life, cyclic retribution seems plausible; what is near is despised and what is far exalted.

sentences.zh: 鞮譯差殊，不可研詰。

translations.literal: Transliteration from the barbarian tongue differed and was disparate; it could not be closely examined and questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarian transliteration varied so widely it could not be rigorously examined.

sentences.zh: 華人之譎誕者，又攘莊周、列禦寇之說佐其高，層累架騰，直出其表，以無上不可加為勝，妄相誇脅而倡其風。

translations.literal: Among Chinese, the crafty and extravagant further seized Zhuang Zhou and Lie Yukou's doctrines to assist its elevation, piling layer upon layer and soaring upward, straight out beyond its bounds, taking 'nothing higher, nothing to be added' as victory, falsely boasting and coercing one another to champion its wind.
translations.idiomatic: Crafty Chinese literati seized on Zhuang Zhou and Lie Yukou to raise it higher still, piling doctrine upon doctrine until it soared beyond measure, taking 'nothing higher can be added' as triumph, and falsely boasting and bullying one another to spread its fashion.

sentences.zh: 於是，自天子逮庶人，皆震動而祠奉之。

translations.literal: Thereupon from the Son of Heaven down to commoners, all were shaken and sacrificed to it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon, from the Son of Heaven to commoners, all were stirred to worship it.

sentences.zh: 初，宰相王縉以緣業事佐代宗，於是始作內道場，晝夜梵唄，冀禳寇戎，大作盂蘭，肖祖宗像，分供塔廟，為賊臣嘻笑。

translations.literal: At the beginning Chancellor Wang Jin, because of karmic affairs assisting Emperor Daizong, then first made inner cloister chapels, day and night Sanskrit chanting, hoping to avert invading enemies, greatly performing Ullambana, shaping ancestral images, distributing offerings to pagodas and temples—making rebel ministers laugh.
translations.idiomatic: Early on Chancellor Wang Jin, pursuing karmic rites under Daizong, first established inner cloister chapels with day-and-night chanting to ward off invaders, staged great Ullambana rites, fashioned ancestral images, and distributed offerings to pagodas and temples—much to the amusement of rebel ministers.

sentences.zh: 至憲宗世，遂迎佛骨於鳳翔，內之宮中。

translations.literal: Reaching Emperor Xianzong's age, they then welcomed the Buddha's relic from Fengxiang and housed it within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: By Xianzong's reign the Buddha's relic was brought from Fengxiang into the palace.

sentences.zh: 韓愈指言其弊，帝怒，竄愈瀕死，憲亦弗獲天年。

translations.literal: Han Yu pointed out its harms; the emperor was angry and exiled Yu nearly to death; Xian also did not obtain his natural years.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu pointed out the harm; the emperor in rage exiled him nearly to death, and Xianzong likewise did not live out his years.

sentences.zh: 幸福而禍，無亦左乎！

translations.literal: Fortune yet calamity—is this not perverse!
translations.idiomatic: Fortune turning to calamity—is that not perverse!

sentences.zh: 懿宗不君，精爽奪迷，復蹈前車而覆之。

translations.literal: Yizong was no true ruler; his spirit was seized and deluded; he again trod the overturned cart of those before.
translations.idiomatic: Yizong was no true ruler; his spirit was seized by delusion, and he repeated the overturned precedent of his predecessors.

sentences.zh: 興哀無知之場，丐庇百解之胔，以死自誓，無有顧藉，流淚拜伏，雖事宗廟上帝，無以進焉。

translations.literal: He raised mourning in a field without knowledge, begged shelter from a corpse of a hundred joints, swore himself by death without regard or restraint, wept and bowed prostrate—even in serving the ancestral temple and High God he could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: He raised mourning in ignorance, begged shelter from a relic of a hundred joints, swore himself to death without restraint, wept and prostrated himself—yet could not advance even the rites owed to the ancestral temple and Heaven.

sentences.zh: 屈萬乘之貴，自等於古胡，數千載而遠，以身為徇。

translations.literal: He bent the dignity of the myriad chariots, equating himself with ancient barbarians thousands of years distant, offering his person as sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He humbled the dignity of the throne, equating himself with barbarians of ages past, and offered his person as sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，運祚殫，天告之矣！

translations.literal: Alas, the mandate was exhausted—Heaven had announced it!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the mandate was spent; Heaven had announced it!

sentences.zh: 懿不三月而徂，唐德之不競，厥有來哉，悲夫！

translations.literal: Yi was gone within three months; Tang virtue's failure to contend—its source lies here—how sad!
translations.idiomatic: Yizong was gone within three months. That Tang virtue could no longer contend had its source here—how lamentable!
